summary: Kenya has no dedicated digital nomad visa. Remote workers use the Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) for stays up to 90 days. No formal remote work program has been announced.

program.verificationNote: Confirmed: Kenya Directorate of Immigration Services lists Work Permit classes A through M, none of which cover remote work for foreign employers. The eTA (Electronic Travel Authorisation) handles most tourist and short-stay visits.

keyFacts: No digital nomad visa program as of November 2026
eTA (Electronic Travel Authorisation) available for tourist stays up to 90 days
Nairobi is a major tech and startup hub with strong coworking infrastructure
Kenya has very good international fiber connectivity
Watch immigration.go.ke for any future program
whyItMatters: Kenya is East Africa's tech capital. Nairobi's iHub, Westlands coworking scene, and fast LTE/fiber coverage make it a practical remote work base. The 90-day eTA covers shorter stays; longer-term arrangements require a different visa strategy.
